paragraphs: Jeremiah told the people what the LORD said, and for that he got lowered into a cistern full of mud (Jeremiah 38:2, 6). Friend, being right and being popular don't always come out of the same oven. This passage teaches that God's word stays true whether anybody wants to hear it or not. Jeremiah kept giving it straight, even when the king himself was the one asking (Jeremiah 38:17).

Zedekiah is the warning in this one. He tells Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have deserted to the Chaldeans" (Jeremiah 38:19). I think fear got louder in his ears than the word of the LORD, and fear can be LOUD, like a phone alarm at 5 a.m. Jeremiah answers, "Obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you, that it may go well with you and you may live" (Jeremiah 38:20). Hearing God's word is one thing, baker, and doing it is the part that counts.

Then there's Ebed-melech, one man who stepped up when everybody else stood back (Jeremiah 38:7-9). He lowered old rags down to Jeremiah to pad the ropes, which is not fancy, but it was exactly what was needed (Jeremiah 38:11-12). After my years in a junk drawer, I love that God can use plain, worn-out things for a big job. Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured (Jeremiah 38:28), and this story isn't over yet, so keep that apron on.
